findings.issue_text: [BUG] `{{#unless automatic}}` evaluates `automatic` on the member User object, not on the group, so it is always falsy and the remove link renders for automatic groups. On automatic groups (admins, staff, trust levels) the remove link appears; clicking it issues DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members which the backend rejects with 422 can_not_modify_automatic, and the admin sees a broken silent-failure UI on every automatic group page.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is one too high whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. A group with 100 members and limit 50 reports 3 pages; clicking next past the real data shows "3/3" with an empty member list because the server returns zero members for offset 100, and showingLast is only reached on the phantom page.

[BUG] The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test issues xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route is only defined as DELETE members => groups#remove_member. The spec raises an ActionDispatch/ActionController routing error (no PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members route) and the suite fails red at this example, masking the 422 assertion it is supposed to make.

[BUG] The public members template now iterates `{{#each m in members}}` while the route sets the controller's model to the Group object, and `members` is only ever set on the Group model after findMembers resolves — it is not a property the GroupMembersController exposes. Unless the GroupMembersController is an ObjectController-style proxy to its model (previously its model was the members array itself, so `model` was the safe binding), the each loop binds to undefined and the public group members page renders an empty table; even with proxying there is a flash of empty content because findMembers is fire-and-forget in setupController.

[BUG] The rewritten templates rely on a `{{fa-icon}}` Handlebars helper while the rest of this codebase era emits icons via raw `<i class='fa fa-...'>` markup (the diff itself deletes exactly such markup at the delete button). If the fa-icon helper is not registered in this revision's Discourse helpers, Ember renders 'Unable to find helper fa-icon' in the admin group page for the pagination controls and the delete/trash/plus icons, breaking the admin group UI on load.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten public members endpoint (new response envelope with meta.total/limit/offset and default limit 50 instead of 200) has no spec coverage anywhere in the diff. A regression in the pagination math (e.g. offset handling or meta totals) would ship uncaught and silently truncate the public group member list for every non-admin user; the JS client consumes result.meta directly so any envelope change breaks paging with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] removeMember/addMembers issue requests to '/admin/groups/:id/members.json' but Discourse.ajax data for DELETE requests is sent as a request body with no explicit contentType, and jQuery does not URL-encode DELETE bodies the way Rails params parsing expects without form encoding. If the body is sent as application/x-www-form-urlencoded with charset handling issues (typical for this-era Discourse.ajax DELETE+data), params.require(:user_id) in remove_member raises ActionController::ParameterMissing (400) instead of removing the member; the bootbox confirm flow then reloads nothing and the admin believes the member was removed.

[ADVISORY] findMembers clamps offset against the stale user_count (initialized to 0 on the model) before the first load, and next/previous read offset/limit/user_count directly off the model that the public group route and admin route share. After the server reports a smaller total (members removed elsewhere), the client's offset can point past the end of the list and the UI shows an empty page with currentPage > totalPages until a full reload; two routes mutating the same model instance also means navigating between admin and public group views reuses a model carrying a mutated offset.

[BUG] totalPages computes floor(user_count/limit)+1, producing a phantom page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. A group with exactly 100 members and limit 50 shows 'x/3'; the admin can navigate to page 3, findMembers sends offset=100 (clamped by Math.min to user_count), and the member list renders empty while the pager claims 3 pages exist.

[BUG] The next action clamps offset to Math.min(offset+limit, user_count) instead of the last page's offset, so the final reachable offset can equal user_count. When user_count is a multiple of limit, the last 'next' click sets offset=user_count (e.g. 100 for 100 users, limit 50), the API returns an empty members array, and the admin sees a blank member list with no way to know members still exist.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips usernames that don't match any user (`if user = User.find_by_username(username)`), while addMembers in the client reloads and shows success. An admin who typos a username in the add-members box gets no error at all — the member list simply doesn't change, and the partially-successful additions are indistinguishable from a total failure; the removed PATCH-era spec 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' shows this behavior was known and is now unverified client-side.

[ADVISORY] The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec issues xhr :put, :remove_member although the route and client both use DELETE, and controller specs bypass routing so the verb mismatch is never caught. The test exercises remove_member via a verb that the production routes.rb never maps to it (delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"), so a routing regression on the DELETE verb — the exact verb the frontend uses — passes the suite.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten public members endpoint (new pagination, new meta envelope, new default limit of 50) has no spec coverage anywhere in the diff — the old TODO-limit behavior for automatic groups is replaced and no GroupsController spec is added or updated. A regression in the offset/limit math or the meta.total value breaks both the admin group pager and the public group members page with no failing test; also the endpoint previously returned an unpaginated array for non-automatic groups, so any out-of-tree consumer parsing the array response now breaks silently on the new {members, meta} shape.

[ADVISORY] addMembers leaves the stale usernames string in the input after adding (acknowledged by the inline TODO), and the promise from model.addMembers is not returned so the button gives no pending state. An admin who clicks Add twice re-submits the same username list; on the server the duplicate group.add is a no-op, but combined with the silent skip of unknown usernames the admin cannot tell whether their action had any effect.

[ADVISORY] update no longer guards alias_level/visible writes with an automatic-group check, and the update spec only verifies that name is ignored for automatic groups — changing alias_level or visible on an automatic group is now exercised by no spec and silently permitted. The old code path returned 403 for automatic groups on PATCH; now an admin PUT with alias_level=99 on group id 1 (admins) persists the change with a success response, and if that behavior is unintended (the old comment said automatic groups 'do not permit membership changes' — it only prohibited membership) nothing in the suite would catch either outcome.

[BUG] add_members and remove_member read params[:group_id], but the routes are declared as member routes under `resources :groups` so the segment param is :id, making params.require(:group_id) raise ActionController::ParameterMissing and return a 500 on every real request. The JS client calls PUT /admin/groups/{id}/members.json; Rails populates params[:id], not :group_id, so every add/remove member request from the UI crashes with a 500 instead of the success/422 contract. The specs only pass because they explicitly pass group_id as a query param.

[BUG] The public group members page now iterates `{{#each m in members}}` but group-members.js.es6's setupController sets `model` (the Group) and never defines a `members` property on the controller, so the loop binds to undefined and renders an empty table. Non-admin users visiting /groups/{name}/members see an empty member list — a regression on a page the PR's stated intent (admin membership handling) does not cover; the template was changed from the working `model` binding to a broken `members` binding with no corresponding controller change in this diff.

[BUG] totalPages computes floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which over-counts by one page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 users, limit 50 → 3 pages with page 3 empty), and the `next` action's clamp `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)` produces offset == user_count on the last real page, requesting a beyond-end page. Admin paging through a group whose member count is divisible by 50 lands on an empty 'extra' page and `showingLast` never becomes true via the intended page math; the count/count check is only masked when the server echoes back a clamped offset.

[BUG] The remove_member specs issue `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route added in config/routes.rb maps remove_member to DELETE, so the request hits no route and the assertions test a 404-fixture path rather than the action. `it "cannot remove members from automatic groups"` asserts response.status == 422 against a PUT that never reaches the controller — the spec fails (or passes only by accident of error status collision), giving false coverage of the new endpoint.

[BUG] findMembers now returns bare `undefined` when the group name is empty instead of the previous Ember.RSVP.resolve([]), so callers that chain .then (e.g. any code doing group.findMembers().then(...)) crash with 'Cannot read property then of undefined'. setupController in admin_group_route.js and group-members.js.es6 call model.findMembers() without guarding; while they don't chain today, the public contract of the model method regressed from always-promise to sometimes-undefined with no requirement driving it.

[ADVISORY] The PATCH-based incremental membership update path (update_patch, with its automatic-group 403 guard) is deleted along with its route behavior and tests, silently breaking any existing client using PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes[add]/changes[delete]. Out-of-tree scripts or older frontends still issuing PATCH updates now fall through to the update action, which silently ignores the `changes` payload and returns success_json — membership appears saved but nothing changed; this is a silent public-surface change not traceable to the stated intent.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips usernames that don't match any user (User.find_by_username returns nil, iteration continues) and still returns success_json, so admins get no feedback that a member was not added. An admin who typos a username in the add-members box sees the list reload with the user absent and no error, and must diff the member list manually to notice; the old UI at least round-tripped the full username list.

[ADVISORY] The relocated .form-horizontal rules are scoped to `.groups, .badges` — the `.badges` scope is unrelated to this PR's stated intent of group membership handling. Badge admin styling silently changes (labels become bold, inputs become 350px) as a side effect of a group-membership fix; anyone debugging badge layout drift must trace it back to this PR, and reverting the group fix would unexpectedly revert badge styling too.

[ADVISORY] This file's changes are pure whitespace re-indentation with no behavioral content, as are the blank-line removals in admin-group-selector.hbs — untraceable churn unrelated to the membership fix. Reviewers and git-blame archaeologists on the autocomplete template must read a 25-line whitespace diff to confirm nothing changed, increasing the cost of every future review of that file.

[ADVISORY] addMembers fires model.addMembers(usernames) but never clears the usernames input or disables the button, leaving the typed names in the selector after the member list reloads (the TODO comment acknowledges this). An admin who double-clicks Add or edits the stale selection submits the same usernames again / adds unintended users on the next click; every admin who uses the new UI hits this immediately.

[BUG] The `{{#unless automatic}}` guard resolves `automatic` on the member User object (the each-item context), not on the group, so the remove link renders for automatic groups too. For automatic groups the members section (rendered under `{{#if id}}` regardless of automatic) shows a working-looking remove link; clicking it sends DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members which the controller rejects with 422 can_not_modify_automatic, leaving the member in the list after every attempt. Users don't have an `automatic` property, so the guard is always falsy.

[BUG] The public GET /groups/:group_name/members response shape changed from a bare serialized array to an envelope {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} with no versioning or compatibility layer. Any existing consumer of this endpoint (plugins, themes, API scripts, mobile/alternate clients) that iterates the JSON array directly — e.g. `JSON.parse(body).each` — now gets a Hash and either crashes or silently iterates nothing, since the diff updated only its own Ember client.

[BUG] The admin group update action switched from the params[:group][...] envelope to flat top-level params, silently discarding fields sent in the old envelope. Existing API clients (admin scripts, plugins, older cached front-end assets during a rolling deploy) that PUT {group: {name: ..., visible: ...}} get a 200 success while name/visible/alias_level are never applied — the group is silently unchanged, because `params[:name]` is nil and `params[:visible] == "true"` evaluates false with no error surfaced.

[ADVISORY] add_members silently skips unknown usernames via `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` and returns success_json regardless, so a typo'd username is dropped with no error. An admin who types a misspelled username into the add-members box gets a success response and a reloaded member list that simply lacks the user, with no indication anything was ignored; the old usernames= path on update went through group validation that at least round-tripped the resulting membership.

[ADVISORY] `usernames.split(",")` assumes a string; `params.require(:usernames)` returns whatever the client sent, and an array payload (usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b, the natural jQuery/Rails array form) makes .split raise NoMethodError. Any client posting the usernames as an array gets a 500 from a member-management endpoint instead of a 4xx; the spec only exercises the comma-joined string form, so the array path is untested.

[ADVISORY] currentPage/totalPages and the next/previous offset clamp consume user_count from the admin groups index payload, which is only refreshed by findMembers, so pagination math runs on a stale count until the first members fetch resolves. For a group whose membership changed since the admin group list was loaded, the first render shows wrong total pages and `next` clamps offset against the stale user_count (e.g. disallows advancing to a page that now exists); it self-corrects only after the async findMembers lands, and offset persisting across add/remove via the meta echo can strand the view on a page past the new end.

[BUG] The public group members page now renders only `members`, which findMembers caps at the default limit of 50, with no pagination controls on this route. The pre-existing user-facing intent — the front-end group page listing all of a group's members — is silently dropped: groups with more than 50 members show a truncated list and users have no way to view members past the first 50.

[BUG] The `get "users"` route on admin groups is deleted and the PATCH-based incremental membership endpoint (`update` with `changes: {add/delete}`) is removed with no replacement path. Any existing API client or integration performing `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes` or `GET /admin/groups/:id/users` now receives a 404/unsupported-action error — a silent public-surface removal during what was framed as a fix, not an API break.

[BUG] totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which yields an extra empty page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, and next() sets offset to min(offset+limit, user_count) so it can navigate onto that empty page. For a group with exactly 50 members, the admin UI shows "1/2" and clicking next fetches offset=50, rendering an empty member list instead of disabling pagination at page 1.

[ADVISORY] The original intent that group creation can set initial members in one atomic request (create with usernames) is dropped: create now accepts only name/visible, and addMembers is a separate PUT that requires an existing group id. Admin clients that created a group with members via one POST now must do two requests, and any failure between create and add_members leaves a half-configured group; also the front-end new-group form gives no way to add members until after the first save.

[ADVISORY] The whole set of incremental add/delete behaviors (including the four 'succeeds silently on nonexistent users / non-members' cases and the 403-on-automatic-PATCH case) is deleted from the controller spec rather than migrated to the new add_members/remove_member endpoints. The documented silent-skip semantics for nonexistent usernames in add_members is now untested, so a future change to raise on unknown users would pass CI while breaking the admin UI's add-members flow whenever a typo'd username is submitted.

[ADVISORY] Automatic-group protection semantics changed from the old update path (raising InvalidAccess/403 for membership changes, ignoring rename) to silently accepting the update request with only the name filtered out. Clients relying on a 403 to detect attempts to modify automatic groups now get a 200 success even though nothing was applied, masking failed operations; the intent 'automatic groups do not permit membership changes' is enforced only on the new endpoints.

[ADVISORY] The public groups#members endpoint accepts a completely unvalidated params[:limit] with no upper bound, so any logged-in user can pass limit=10000000 and have the full member list of any visible group serialized in one response. An anonymous/authenticated user enumerates every username, avatar URL, and last_seen timestamp of any visible (including large automatic) group in a single request, enabling bulk user-enumeration scraping that the previous 200-hard-cap-for-automatic-groups behavior throttled, and a large limit on a huge group (e.g. trust_level groups) causes a heavy DB query and serialization spike per request — a cheap DoS amplification vector.

[ADVISORY] add_members calls usernames.split(",") after params.require(:usernames), which raises NoMethodError (500) when usernames arrives as an array (Rails parses repeated params or user[]-style submissions as Array) instead of a comma string. Any admin (or a crafted multipart form from an admin session) sending usernames[]=a sends Array into .split, producing a 500 instead of a 4xx; the member list is not modified but the request is unhandled, and the 500 leaks a stack trace in non-production configs.

[ADVISORY] remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) with no existence check and then relies on group.save, so deleting a non-existent or non-member user_id silently reports success_json with no mutation, and group.save on an automatic-guarded path has already deleted rows before the guard could matter if ordering changed. Admin clients cannot distinguish 'removed member' from 'user never existed / was not a member', masking data errors; more importantly the delete executes via the association before any save-time validation, so future changes to the automatic-group guard placed after the delete would fire too late while still returning an error status.

[ADVISORY] update mutates alias_level and visible on automatic groups (only the name change is guarded), and the guard is a comment-only invariant for name, so the previous Discourse::InvalidAccess protection for automatic-group changes is now limited to membership endpoints only. An admin can flip alias_level/visibility of system automatic groups (e.g. staff, trust_level_0) via the generic update endpoint, altering who may interact with those groups' trust semantics — a misconfiguration surface that previously raised 403 for automatic-group membership changes and now has an inconsistent, undocumented policy.

[ADVISORY] The only '.update' test covers the automatic-group path; the non-automatic rename path (group.name = params[:name] when !group.automatic, app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb line ~35) has no test in the diff after the old 'able to update group members' test was deleted. A regression in non-automatic group renaming (e.g. dropping the !group.automatic guard in the other direction, or name validation) ships silently; the old spec verified rename-to-'fred' and was replaced by a single automatic-group test, so the primary user-facing branch of update is now unverified.

[ADVISORY] The '.create' test only exercises the success path; the render_json_error branch for an invalid group (blank/invalid name) added in this diff's create action is never triggered by any test. The error-handling branch that returns validation errors is untested; if render_json_error(group) is wired wrong (wrong status, wrong payload), the admin UI shows a silent failure and no test catches it. Checked the diff: the only .create tests are 'strip spaces on the group name' (happy path).

[ADVISORY] add_members' silent-skip branch for non-existent usernames (the `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` nil case in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb) is untested — the diff deleted the old 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' test without porting it to the new endpoint. The new endpoint returns success_json while silently dropping unknown usernames; an admin who typos a name gets 'success' with no member added and no test documents or verifies that behavior, so a future change to surface an error (or to break it) goes unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] The automatic-group update test asserts only `group.name.should_not == "WAT"` — a negative assertion that would pass if the name were changed to any other wrong value. If the guard `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic` mutated the name to anything other than the literal 'WAT' (e.g. downcased, truncated, or set via another path), the test still passes; asserting `group.name.should == "admins"` (the seed name of group 1) would actually pin the preserved value.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten public members endpoint — pagination via limit/offset params and the new members/meta JSON envelope that the frontend's findMembers() depends on (result.meta.total, result.meta.limit, result.meta.offset) — is exercised by no test in this diff. The admin group page's pagination state is driven entirely by this meta shape; a serializer change or a wrong key breaks the whole member list, and the old GroupUserSerializer-array contract test was not replaced. No spec file for groups_controller (public) appears anywhere in the diff, so this server-behavior change ships with zero verification.

[BUG] remove_member passes a raw user id (params.require(:user_id).to_i) to group.users.delete, but an ActiveRecord association delete expects User instances, not integers. Deleting a member from the admin UI raises (ActiveRecord raises an "expected User, got Fixnum"-style error) — the DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members.json request 500s and the member is never removed; the spec that passes does so only because group.save after the exception-free path is not actually exercised against a real id-typed delete in this shape.

[ADVISORY] findMembers now returns undefined (bare `return;`) when the group name is empty, instead of the resolved promise the old code returned. Any caller chaining .then/.catch off findMembers (the removed route afterModel used to) gets 'Cannot read property then of undefined'; today setupController fire-and-forgets, but a nil-promise return from a shared model method is a trap for the next caller, and during the page load no error state is surfaced when name is blank.

[ADVISORY] The update action drops all handling of params[:group][:usernames] / params[:changes] that the previous update_put/update_patch supported, while the route and endpoint are kept. Any client or API consumer still on the old payload shape (grouped params or PATCH changes add/delete) during a rolling deploy silently loses membership edits — the server 200s with success_json while persisting no membership change — a dual-write gap with no versioned endpoint for the old contract.

[ADVISORY] The members template now iterates `members` instead of `model`, but the route sets controller model to the group and only findMembers' async callback populates the group's `members` property. The /g/:name/members page renders an empty list until the ajax resolves (and blank forever if the request fails, since the error path never sets `members`); on slow networks users see an empty member list that looks like the group has no members — data that exists appears lost.

[BUG] add_members silently skips usernames that don't match any user and still renders success_json, so the admin client reports the add as complete while work was dropped. An admin pastes a list with one typo'd or deleted username; the API returns 200 success, the client clears nothing and reloads the member list, and the missing member is invisible — no error, no log, no indication which username failed. The old test even codified this ('succeeds silently when adding non-existent users'); the new diff preserves the drop but removed all coverage of it.

[BUG] Pagination math produces an empty last page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit, because totalPages = floor(count/limit) + 1 unconditionally. A group with exactly 50 members and limit 50 gets totalPages = 2 and the 'next' action is enabled (showingLast is false since currentPage 1 != 2); clicking next sets offset = min(50, 50) = 50 and fetches a page past the end, showing the admin an empty member list for page '2/2' with user_count 50.

[ADVISORY] The member-list reload after addMembers and removeMember is fire-and-forget inside the .then callback: `self.findMembers();` is neither returned nor given a rejection handler, so the outer promise resolves success before the reload completes. If the reload request fails (network drop, 500), the ajax promise from addMembers/removeMember has already resolved and the rejection is unhandled: the admin sees the member list silently remain stale after the action 'succeeded', with no error surfaced anywhere.

[ADVISORY] remove_member persists the deletion via `group.users.delete(user_id)` before the `group.save` whose result determines the response, and it returns success for a user_id that was never a member. The join row is destroyed by `group.users.delete` regardless of what `group.save` does afterwards, so a save failure still reports an error while the removal already happened; conversely removing a non-member user_id returns 200 success with no change made, hiding client-side user_id staleness (e.g. a member removed in another tab) from the admin.

[ADVISORY] addMembers has no in-flight guard and the usernames input is never cleared (the TODO acknowledges it), so rapid double-click of the Add button issues overlapping identical PUT /members requests. An impatient admin double-clicks Add; two overlapping add_members requests fire, each iterating usernames and calling group.add — concurrent add/save on the same Group row races the has_many join inserts and can raise on the second request, surfacing a spurious error for an action that succeeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The public groups#members endpoint accepts a completely unvalidated params[:limit] with no upper bound, so any logged-in user can pass limit=10000000 and have the full member list of any visible group serialized in one response. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] add_members calls usernames.split(",") after params.require(:usernames), which raises NoMethodError (500) when usernames arrives as an array (Rails parses repeated params or user[]-style submissions as Array) instead of a comma string.
